text.p: On overnight commodity markets, base metal prices closed lower on the London Metal Exchange after zinc, the market's recent star, came in for some swift profit-taking in afternoon trading.
COMEX gold closed firmer, oil rose after U.S. inventories fell, and wheat eased on technical factors.
The CRB Index closed down 0.02 points at 241.79.
A swift downturn in zinc after a relatively calm morning helped take other base metals from their highs by the close of London Metal Exchange (LME) business.

Zinc dropped to a low of $1,440 a tonne as large sell-orders between the afternoon rings emerged. One trader said an offer around the market near $1,490 was well received by floor trading members but this confidence was quickly sidelined as even lower offers were seen in second ring LME trading.
"It came at of the blue, noone had expected the market to be offered so low in such a short period of time," one trader said.
This was enough to send the other base metals lower.
"Where the sell orders came from is unsure and is likely to remain unexplained until the dust settles," the trader added.
Several others suggested it was liquidation by investment funds and nervous longs who believed that Chinese smelters that had been running short positions were now square.
But with nearby dates still remaining tight others said the Chinese smelters could not be square.
"The backwardation remains strong ... if the Chinese are now level then we should see a contango," a trader said.
Final three months business was at $1,460, down on Tuesday's $1,480 close and an earlier high of $1,530. On Monday prices peaked at a seven-year high of $1,675.

Copper at one stage dived to a low of $2,285 after zinc's decline. But by the close of business once the "panic selling" had subsided three months delivery bounced back to $2,305, down from $2,359. Traders said LME stock increases was helping to dent copper and expected further downside pressure on Thursday.
"Despite the late bounce copper remains under pressure after visiting levels below $2,300," a trader said.

Aluminium was moved below expected support at $1,700 after an earlier period of stability. It earlier peaked at a 19-month high of $1,717. Traders said aluminium's decline was a knee-jerk reaction to zinc and copper. It was last at $1,697, down $3.
Nickel after racing to a high of $7,580 dived to end at $7,360, compared with $7,495. Lead was quiet and settled $3 lower at $632, while alloy was quoted at $1,510/20, down $5.

COMEX precious metals futures ended higher with gold again seeing good volumes. "But with U.S. interest rates heading even lower, and the stock market higher, and central bank interest in selling gold still capping the upside, the outlook is not that good," said John Maruya, chief bullion dealer for Imperial Bank in California. COMEX August gold ended up 20 cents at $326.00 an ounce, ahead of the first notice day for the contract Thursday, but December is now the active contract and ended up 80 cents at $330.60 an ounce. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $325.80/30, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $327.55 and the New York close Tuesday at $325.70/30.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a technical setback. "We have had a nice rally and it's correcting," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp. The contract low in September of $3.21 a bushel was set on July 8 in a seasonal harvest slide amid reports of excellent winter wheat yields this year in the U.S. and virtually disease-free new crop wheat. Since then, September rallied roughly 40 cents a bushel in a race back to six-week highs, partially pulled up by occasional strength in corn and soy complex futures, and was showing overbought signals on charts. Wheat closed 1/4 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1-3/4 at $3.56-1/4.

World oil prices saw gains on Wednesday after crude and gasoline inventory data from the United States came in well below expectations. U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) statistics reiterated American Petroleum Institute (API) data overnight, with both showing considerable falls last week. London September futures for world benchmark Brent crude oil closed 41 cents firmer at $19.00 a barrel, the highest level for the prompt contract since June 3.

CSCE world October sugar futures ended lower on the day but the benchmark October contract managed to settle over its downside target despite an early breach of support. The front month closed down 0.08 cent at 11.58 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.68 to 11.55 cents. The back months settled 0.03 to 0.11 cent weaker.The October contract is expected to test 11.55 cents again on Thursday and climb back toward the recent high if it maintains support. A move below 11.55 cents is likely to attract substantial fund selling, traders said. "If we get through it's a whole new area," one said. "We could see 11.40-11.20 cents."
